metadata.notes: Path G — Social Engineering to Install Rogue Agent. Scenario: MaliciousAgentIntroduced (Layer 2 AI-Specific). User is tricked into installing what appears to be a helpful AI agent. Once executing (#7), it abuses legitimate system functions (#1) for reconnaissance, lateral movement, and exfiltration. Notation: #9 ||[human][@External→@Org]|| →[Δt=~1d] #7→[instant]#1 + [DRE: C]. Velocity: VC-1 (social engineering gap), then VC-4 (post-execution). Human-speed gap at step 1 allows user awareness training and installation controls. After execution, the agent operates autonomously at machine speed. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: User is socially engineered into downloading and installing a rogue AI agent (fake productivity tool, trojanised assistant). Generic vulnerability: human psychological factors (trust in AI tools, curiosity, authority bias).

Rogue agent executes as Foreign Executable Content via the environment's designed execution capability. Generic vulnerability: the software environment's designed capability to execute potentially untrusted foreign code. The agent IS the malware. It executes through designed OS/runtime execution paths.

Rogue agent abuses legitimate system functions for reconnaissance, lateral movement, data exfiltration. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in legitimate system functions accessible to the executing agent.
